findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password check
findings.body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` (line 131) is entered even when a totpCode is also present. An attacker who obtains a single valid backup code can send `{"email":victim, "totpCode":"anything", "backupCode":valid}`: the password check is skipped because totpCode is truthy, and the backup-code check then succeeds without ever verifying the password. This reduces login to single-factor possession of a long-lived backup code and allows account takeover without the password.

findings.title: Used backup codes nulled with no regeneration, leading to lockout
findings.body: In packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts a consumed backup code is replaced with `null` and re-encrypted, so after 10 uses the stored value is `[null,...]`. The check `if (!user.backupCodes)` never becomes true again, so `MissingBackupCodes` is never returned; further backup attempts return `IncorrectBackupCode`. There is no endpoint to regenerate codes while 2FA is enabled (setup rejects with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled). A user who loses their authenticator and exhausts codes is permanently locked out with a misleading error.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode crashes disable endpoint
findings.body: In apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts line 61 calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-","")` unconditionally once the truthy branch is taken, with no type check. If the client sends a non-string truthy value (number, object, array) this throws TypeError, uncaught, producing a 500 instead of a 400 validation error. The same unsafe call exists for login. It also throws `new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` for missing key/secret (lines 51,77,82) instead of returning `res.status(500).json()`, breaking the client's `response.json()` error handling.

findings.title: Backup codes and secret not cleared on reset, stale sensitive data retained
findings.body: In apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx `resetState()` only clears password, error and step, but leaves `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `dataUri` and `secret` in state. If the modal is cancelled after codes are fetched and reopened, the previous user's secret and backup codes remain in memory and the old object URL is never revoked, leaking sensitive 2FA material across sessions and leaking Blob URLs.
